faq.q: How much weight do people lose on the Wegovy pill?
faq.a: In the OASIS 4 trial, adults without diabetes on the 25 mg pill lost 13.6 percent of their body weight at 64 weeks across everyone enrolled, and close to 17 percent among those who stayed on treatment, versus about 2 to 3 percent on placebo.

faq.q: How do you take the Wegovy pill?
faq.a: Once a day, first thing in the morning, on an empty stomach with a small sip of plain water, then wait about 30 minutes before eating, drinking anything else or taking other medications. The dose steps up over several months from 1.5 mg to 4, 9 and finally 25 mg. Follow the label and your prescriber's instructions.

faq.q: How much does the Wegovy pill cost?
faq.a: Novo Nordisk's self-pay prices are $149 a month for the 1.5 mg starting dose, $199 for 4 mg, and $299 for the 9 mg and 25 mg doses. Insurance coverage varies, and eligible Medicare Part D members may qualify for a $50 copay through the GLP-1 Bridge program.

Both are daily pills approved for weight loss in 2026. The Wegovy pill produced somewhat more weight loss in its trial (13.6 versus 11.1 percent) but requires the empty-stomach, 30-minute routine every morning. Foundayo can be taken with or without food. Prices overlap. Your prescriber can help you weigh adherence against the trial numbers.

bottom_line: The Wegovy pill is the same semaglutide that works in the shot, in a tablet that costs less and asks for a strict morning routine in exchange. It lost a little less weight in trials than the injection and a little more than Foundayo. For people who will not inject, or who want the cheapest way into a proven molecule, it is a real option. For people who can do a weekly shot, the injection remains the stronger tool. The eating rules do not change with the delivery method: small meals, protein first, track it.
body_html:
On December 22, 2025 the FDA approved the first GLP-1 pill for weight loss, and on January 5, 2026 it went on sale at $149 a month for the starting dose. The Wegovy pill is oral semaglutide at a 25 mg maintenance dose, the same molecule as the Wegovy shot and Ozempic, formulated to survive the stomach. It is a big deal for one simple reason: a lot of people who would never inject will swallow a tablet. This review covers what it does, what it costs, the routine it demands, and where it sits against the shot and the newer Foundayo pill.

What the Wegovy Pill Is and Who It Is For

It is a once-daily tablet approved for chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition, alongside diet and activity. Dosing steps up from 1.5 mg to 4 mg to 9 mg and finally 25 mg, with each step lasting at least four weeks. Because semaglutide is poorly absorbed from the gut, the pill uses an absorption enhancer and has to be taken under strict conditions to work: first thing in the morning, empty stomach, a small sip of plain water, then nothing to eat or drink for about 30 minutes. Skip the wait and you absorb much less of the dose.

What It Did in Trials

  • OASIS 4 (25 mg, 64 weeks, no diabetes): 13.6 percent average body-weight loss across everyone enrolled, versus 2.4 percent on placebo. Among people who stayed on treatment, close to 17 percent versus about 3 percent.
  • Compared with the shot: Wegovy 2.4 mg injection averaged about 15 percent in STEP 1 and 20.7 percent at the 7.2 mg HD dose. The pill lands below both.
  • Compared with Foundayo: Foundayo averaged 11.1 percent across everyone in ATTAIN-1 at 72 weeks, so the Wegovy pill has the edge on trial weight loss between the two tablets.

Cost in 2026

Novo Nordisk priced the pill below its injections from the start. Self-pay through NovoCare is $149 a month for 1.5 mg, $199 for 4 mg, and $299 for the 9 mg and 25 mg doses. That makes the first few months the cheapest entry into a proven GLP-1 available. Insurance coverage for the pill is still developing plan by plan, and eligible Medicare Part D members may pay a $50 copay through the GLP-1 Bridge program that started July 1, 2026. Confirm current pricing before you plan around it.

The Morning Routine Is the Real Cost

The money is the easy part. The hard part is every single morning: wake up, take the pill with no more than a few ounces of water, and do not eat, drink coffee or take anything else for 30 minutes. People who already take a thyroid pill on an empty stomach know the drill. People who roll out of bed into breakfast find it harder than they expect, and a missed routine is a wasted dose. If that sounds like you, read the Foundayo review before deciding; it can be taken with or without food.

Side Effects

The same semaglutide profile as the shot: nausea around dose increases, constipation, reflux, fatigue, reduced appetite. Some people find the daily pill produces a steadier, lower level of nausea than the weekly injection's peak; others do not notice a difference. The label carries the same rarer serious risks, including pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents. For the food side, see the GLP-1 nausea guide. For anything else, your prescriber.

Eating on the Wegovy Pill

One practical wrinkle: the 30-minute wait pushes breakfast later, and on a GLP-1 a skipped breakfast is 20 grams of protein you will not make up. Plan a small, protein-first breakfast for when the wait ends; the GLP-1 breakfast ideas post is built for exactly that. Otherwise the rules match every GLP-1: small portions, protein first, five small eating windows, and a daily floor near 100 grams so you lose fat and keep muscle. The Wegovy food list applies to the pill just as much as the shot.

Wegovy Pill vs the Alternatives

  • vs the Wegovy shot: the injection loses more weight on average and needs no morning routine; the pill is cheaper and needle-free. See the Wegovy review.
  • vs Foundayo: the Wegovy pill has stronger trial numbers; Foundayo has the easier routine. Prices overlap.
  • vs Zepbound: not close on average weight loss, but $149 versus $299 to $449 is a real gap. The full comparison lines them up.

How People Actually Get the Wegovy Pill in 2026

There are three routes, and the right one depends on your insurance and your diagnosis.

  1. Through your own doctor and insurance. The Wegovy pill is labeled for weight management; plan coverage is still being added, so ask your prescriber and your plan. Ask your prescriber what your plan requires; prior authorization is common.
  2. Self-pay direct from the manufacturer. NovoCare Pharmacy ships the Wegovy pill at $149 to $299 a month by dose. Prices change often, so check the manufacturer's page before you decide.
  3. Through an online weight-loss clinic. A licensed clinician reviews your history by video or questionnaire, prescribes if appropriate, and either sends the prescription to a pharmacy or ships treatment to you. This is the fastest route if your regular doctor will not prescribe for weight loss.
